question:
Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) totally fun first (i.e., Entertainment game reappropriated), 
        (2) mostly fun first (i.e., design workshop with disabled stakeholders),
        (3) both fun and utility first (i.e., design workshop with diverse stakeholders), 
        (4) mostly utility first (i.e., primary utilitarian mechanic designed first),
        (5) totally utility first (i.e., made by clinicians or specialists, fun incorporated later)
reasoning: The system is an automated therapy tool for childhood apraxia of speech, architected by computer/electrical engineers in collaboration with speech therapists and explicitly based on the Nuffield Dyspraxia Program, a clinical intervention protocol. The primary focus is remote administration of structured CAS therapy (client-server architecture, automated speech analysis, clinician UI, NDP3 adherence), with fun/engagement elements (animations, rewards, games) discussed only as later additions based on user feedback, not as the starting point of the design. This matches a totally utility-first, clinician/specialist-driven design with fun incorporated later.

question:
Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) unstructured play (i.e., no rules, making art),
        (2) semi-structured play (i.e., playground activities),
        (3) flexible structure with rules (i.e., improv),
        (4) flexible game (i.e., board game with house rules),
        (5) game with rigid rules (i.e., video game)
reasoning: The therapy app presents specific NDP3 exercises assigned by the therapist, prompts with fixed stimuli, records constrained speech responses, and provides structured feedback. Activities are tightly task-oriented and modeled after standardized face-to-face NDP3 sessions, indicating a highly structured, rule-bound interaction rather than open or flexible play, best matching a game with rigid rules.

question:
Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely skill-based (i.e., trivia, sports),
        (2) mostly skill-based (i.e., mario kart),
        (3) equally skill and chance-based (i.e., catan),
        (4) mostly chance-based (i.e., Uno),
        (5) entirely chance-based (i.e., all dice)
reasoning: The task is speech therapy exercises where children must correctly produce specific sounds, syllables, or words in response to visual stimuli, with feedback and rewards. Outcomes depend on the child’s articulation skill and practice, not random elements. No chance mechanics (dice, cards drawn at random, etc.) are described, so the design is entirely skill-based.

question:
Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely solo (i.e., solitaire),
        (2) mostly solo (i.e., playing against AI in single-player StarCraft),
        (3) mix of solo and social affordances (i.e., animal crossing),
        (4) mostly social, but aspects are independent (i.e., house on hill haunt transition),
        (5) entirely social (i.e., tag)
reasoning: The tablet app is used by a child under supervision of a therapist (social), but the core interaction is the child individually doing exercises, recording and playing back their own speech (solo). The design also targets in-home use where parents may be present but the exercises themselves are individually performed, indicating a mix of solo practice with social/remote-therapist affordances rather than purely solo or purely social.

question:
Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely turn-based (i.e., tic tac toe),
        (2) follows a set of steps (i.e., viticulture's dynamic turn ordering),
        (3) turns are taken, but some actions can be taken at any time (i.e., pandemic),
        (4) most actions can be taken at any time, but there are some phases (i.e., PvP death reset timer),
        (5) entirely simultaneous (i.e., race)
reasoning: The system is a structured therapy app where the child selects a course, then an exercise, then proceeds through stimulus images one by one, recording and playing back utterances. This is a sequential, stepwise interaction modeled after therapist-led sessions, not simultaneous or free-timing; it best matches a design that follows a set of steps rather than turn-based or real-time simultaneous play.

question:
Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely synchronous (i.e., real time strategy game),
        (2) mostly synchronous with a few asynchronous affordances (i.e., league of legends),
        (3) equal mix of synchronous and asynchronous affordances (i.e., helldivers 2),
        (4) mostly asynchronous with few synchronous affordances (i.e. cookie clicker),
        (5) entirely asynchronous (i.e., chess by postage mail)
reasoning: The system is a remote, client-server speech therapy tool where children practice individually on a tablet. They select exercises, record utterances, and uploads occur asynchronously in the background. Therapists remotely assign courses and later review recordings; there is no indication of real-time, synchronous interaction or co-play, so the design is entirely asynchronous.

question:
Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely competitive (i.e., spit card game),
        (2) mostly competitive, but sometimes collaboration is important (i.e., forbidden island),
        (3) mix of competitive and collaborative (i.e., mario party 2 vs 2 mini-games),
        (4) mostly collaborative (i.e., animal crossing),
        (5) entirely collaborative (i.e., pandemic)
reasoning: The system is a speech-therapy app used by a child together with a therapist, modeled directly on traditional therapist–child CAS therapy sessions. There is no mention of multiple players competing, scores, or adversarial mechanics; the focus is entirely on the child practicing and the therapist monitoring and assisting. Any game-like elements (rewards, stars, puzzles) are for engagement and reinforcement, not competition. This is a fully cooperative therapeutic context, so the design is entirely collaborative.

question:
Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely symmetrical (i.e., tic tac toe),
        (2) mostly symmetrical (i.e., undertale's differing NPC behaviors based on previous playthroughs),
        (3) both symmetrical and asymmetrical (i.e., pandemic with its similar turn structure but different character abilities),
        (4) mostly asymmetrical (i.e., tag),
        (5) entirely asymmetrical (i.e., keep talking, nobody explodes)
reasoning: The system structures therapy sessions similarly for all children (same NDP3-based activities, same tablet app workflow), indicating symmetrical turn/interaction structure. However, therapy content is adapted to each child’s individual needs and progress, and each child’s speech disability is unique and requires individualized care, introducing asymmetry in roles and abilities. This matches a design that is both symmetrical and asymmetrical.
